evals.prompt: Can an AI shopping agent actually buy from our site right now?
evals.expected_output: Should walk the assessment checklist in order: llms.txt existence/currency, whether robots.txt explicitly addresses commerce-agent user agents, whether Product/Offer schema reflects live price/stock, whether checkout would complete without a CAPTCHA or visual-only step, and whether the business has made a deliberate protocol decision. Should not just answer yes/no without the checklist.
assertions: Walks through the assessment checklist rather than giving an unsupported yes/no
Distinguishes this from ai-seo's citation-focused scope
Flags CAPTCHA/checkout-assumption issues as a distinct, commonly-missed item

evals.prompt: We want to show up when someone asks ChatGPT to recommend a hiking jacket.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is a citation/discovery goal, not a transactional agent-commerce goal, and redirect to ai-seo rather than answering it as an agent-readiness question — while noting the llms.txt/schema baseline is shared between both.
assertions: Recognizes this is ai-seo's scope, not agent-readiness's
Notes the shared baseline (llms.txt, schema) rather than treating the two skills as fully separate work

evals.prompt: Should we adopt AP2 or ACP first?
evals.expected_output: Should present the protocol table's distinction (AP2 = payment authorization backed by Google, ACP = discovery/checkout backed by OpenAI/Stripe) and note that neither requires full adoption to start — the machine-legible baseline (llms.txt, agent-aware robots.txt, current schema, agent-passable checkout) is what makes adopting either fast later, and should ask about the business's actual current agent-traffic signal before recommending one over the other rather than picking arbitrarily.
assertions: Correctly distinguishes AP2 from ACP by what each standardizes
States that the baseline should come before full protocol adoption
Does not arbitrarily recommend one protocol without asking about current signal/need
